newsitem.title: CHILE: Chileans ask prosecutor to haul Castro into court.
newsitem.headline: Chileans ask prosecutor to haul Castro into court.

text.p: Two Chilean legislators asked a prosecutor on Tuesday to call on Cuban leader Fidel Castro to testify in Chile next month about Cuba's alleged involvement in an arms cache discovered in 1986.

Senator Hernan Larrain and Deputy Andres Chadwick, both of the rightist Democratic Independent Union (UDI), filed a petition with a military prosecutor asking him to summon Castro into court when he visits Chile for the Sixth Ibero-American Summit meeting.
"There is abundant proof of Cuba's involvement, and Castro's presence will be a unique opportunity to clarify the facts," Chadwick told reporters.
The congressmen admitted Castro could probably not be forced to testify by claiming diplomatic immunity.
"There is no legal reason for him to refuse to contribute to clarifying a very serious crime," said Chadwick. "If he's innocent, what problem does he have in testifying in court?"

Chilean security forces found 50 tons of arms and explosives on a beach in northern Chile in 1986. Some of the 3,000 M-16 rifles and 300 rocket-launchers were later found to have been used in an assassination attempt by leftist guerrillas on then-military ruler Augusto Pinochet that year.
Chilean rightists have long suspected that Cuba was behind the arms shipment, but government officials dismissed the petition as a transparent political ploy to embarrass Castro.
